title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: Streaming endpoints have historically been brittle when clients cancel mid-stream or when network disconnects occur. This PR implements a server-side lifecycle control surface to reliably handle client cancel, disconnect, and client reconnect/resume flows, and to enforce sane server-side timeouts to prevent resource leaks.

Scope: 1) API surface additions to expose reconnect/resume tokens and explicit cancel acknowledgements (backwards-compatible with OpenAI-style streaming); 2) server runtime state machine to track stream sessions and enforce per-session timeouts; 3) graceful handling of unexpected disconnects with automatic small-window replay and client resume; 4) compatibility layer changes to preserve OpenAI streaming semantics while enabling stronger lifecycle guarantees; 5) tests and docs.

Design summary: - Introduces a lightweight session id and resume token returned in the initial streaming response headers (compatible with OpenAI compatibility layer; header names are X-Redwood-Session and X-Resume-Token). - Adds explicit "cancel_ack" event that server emits when it has cleaned up resources for a cancelled stream. Clients can rely on this for deterministic cleanup. - Implements a server-side state machine (Opening -> Streaming -> Paused -> Terminated) with configurable timeouts: idle_timeout (client disconnect with no reconnect within window) and ack_timeout (how long server waits for cancel to be acknowledged before force-killing). - On unexpected disconnect, server retains short-lived KV of recent tokens and KV-cache pointer to allow fast resume without full re-execution if the client reconnects within resume_window (configurable, defaults to 30s). - For clients that cannot resume, the server will close streams after idle_timeout and emit metrics and audit log entries. - No behavioral change to tool/function calling or structured output; function-calling inference continues to emit events in-order, and resume always replays the last stable event boundary to guarantee idempotency.

Compatibility notes: - OpenAI compatibility: the streaming frame format remains unchanged; resume token and session header are additive and ignored by vanilla OpenAI clients. - SDKs: JS and Python SDKs expose a StreamingSession helper that automatically handles reconnect and resume. Existing client code using plain stream reading continues to work but won't get automatic resume.

Operational considerations: - New metrics: streaming.session_resume, streaming.session_cancel_ack_latency, streaming.session_idle_killed. Alerts updated to detect elevated idle_killed rates. - Defaults chosen conservatively to avoid increasing cost for idle clients; customers can tune per-route.

Testing: unit tests for state machine; integration tests for disconnect->reconnect and cancel flows; e2e for OpenAI-compat resume. CI flakiness addressed with a retry harness for the integration smoke test (was flaky under heavy host load).

Changelog/Release notes included below.

References: Linear ENG-14209 (streaming lifecycle controls), ENG-14222 (openai compat resume), SUP-7213 (customer-reported disconnects).

review_comments: Evan Martin: Left a few nits on the timeout defaults and suggested making resume_window configurable per-route. Also asked for clearer invariants on what gets replayed on resume (token vs event boundary).
Priya Desai: Responded: widened resume_window to be per-route and clarified that replay is always done at the last stable event boundary (no partial tokens). Added tests for event-boundary semantics.
Daria Kovács: Requested additional metrics for canceled streams and confirm that cancel_ack is emitted before resource deallocation.
Priya Desai: Responded: emit cancel_ack before dealloc and added streaming.session_cancel_ack_latency metric. Updated docs with guidance for operators.
Marco Li: CI auth test flaked once; suggested adding retry wrapper. Priya: added ci/streaming-flaky-retry.yml to reduce flakes.
Evan Martin: Approve after changes. Daria Kovács: Approve. Marco Li: Approve.
